findings.issue_text: Initializer comment references config/initializers/02-freedom_patches.rb which does not exist; the actual ordering guarantee comes from config/application.rb, so the comment misleads maintainers and reordering per it breaks boot

I18n.ensure_loaded! exists only via an out-of-tree monkey patch (translate_accelerator.rb), not the i18n gem, creating a hard undocumented dependency that raises NoMethodError if the patch isn't applied first
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash and overrides [] but not []=, so custom per-locale fallbacks registered via the standard API are silently discarded on every read

SiteSetting.default_locale is evaluated lazily inside [], causing DB/cache access during translation misses which can crash background jobs, mailer deliveries, boot-time plugin calls, and rake tasks on fresh installs

No tests in the diff for a behavior change affecting every translated string: fallback resolution regression could ship undetected, and fallback ordering and environment-level fallback deletion are unverified

FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback resolution with no handling for missing current-site context, breaking boot/migrations/rake jobs that translate before a site scope is established

ensure_loaded! is only invoked on the web-request path, so background jobs, ActionMailer deliveries, MessageBus/SSR paths, and console/rake contexts fall back to slow translate_no_cache/lazy-load per lookup

Locale fallback loading only occurs inside set_locale which runs only for web requests; background jobs, mailers, oneboxes, cron, and console code using I18n.t get missing translations because TranslateAccelerator#translate only loads config.locale

Global I18n.fallbacks assignment in the initializer changes dev/test behavior by enabling fallbacks there, since fallbacks were previously gated to production-like environments via config.i18n.fallbacks in production.rb/profile.rb; this breaks tests asserting missing translations

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! runs on every request and FallbackLocaleList#[] allocates a fresh array and re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale each call, plus the loaded-check and chain-construction are split across two files that must be kept in sync

Subclassing Hash to impersonate I18n.fallbacks only implements the [] method; plugins or Rails upgrades calling defaults, insert, or per-locale mutation (e.g. I18n.fallbacks[:de] = ...) will crash with NoMethodError or TypeError

Fallbacks module included via I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks) is dead code on the hot path because TranslateAccelerator's own class-level translate method shadows the module's translate; fallback only works accidentally via the super chain in translate_no_cache and could silently break on refactor
Fallback behavior should live in TranslateAccelerator (which owns translate) rather than bolted on via include where it is overridden
Process-global cache keyed only by [locale, key] with no site dimension causes cross-site cache poisoning of fallback results in multisite, since default_locale varies per site
FallbackLocaleList Hash subclass silently discards writes: []= and merge! store entries never read back because [] is overridden, so plugin/gem fallback configuration is silently ignored

ensure_loaded! is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, so background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and scripts run fallbacks against unloaded locale data, bypassing the accelerator and leaving @loaded_locales unpopulated
Fallback terminal anchor changed from I18n.default_locale to hardcoded :en, breaking the documented invariant that the site's default locale is the terminal fallback
SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym raises NoMethodError when settings store is not connected at translation time (rake tasks, migrations, early boot), converting missing translations into exceptions
I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, ...) relies on initializer load order enforced only by a comment, so backend replacement (e.g. caching backend) can silently disable fallbacks
Replacing I18n.fallbacks with a Hash subclass breaks the i18n gem Fallbacks API; I18n.t with fallbacks: option raises ArgumentError instead of honoring per-call fallback overrides

FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every fallback lookup, making translation a hard DB dependency that crashes (NoMethodError/ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid) during db:migrate on a fresh DB, assets:precompile without a DB, or rolling deploys before migrations finish, unlike the old static config.i18n.fallbacks = true

Fallback chain changed from static I18n.default_locale (:en) to mutable SiteSetting.default_locale, so admins changing default_locale silently alters fallback text site-wide for every user with no migration, announcement, rollback, or opt-out setting

translate_accelerator.rb's translate method dereferences @loaded_locales directly without the ||= [] guard used in ensure_loaded!, causing NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil if translate is called before ensure_loaded!/load_locale

Fallback locales are only loaded inside the request cycle via set_locale, so fallback lookups outside controllers (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer, console, scripts) silently return 'translation missing' because the accelerator only loads config.locale and never loads fallback locales like :en
FallbackLocaleList overrides Hash#[] to always compute a fresh list, so any code mutating the fallbacks hash (I18n.fallbacks[:de] << :fr or assignment) is silently dropped with no error or effect

ensure_loaded! check-then-act on the shared @loaded_locales array races under multi-threaded request handling; concurrent requests can observe the backend mid-swap, serving missing or double-loaded translations

goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: ensure_loaded! check-then-act on the shared @loaded_locales array races under multi-threaded request handling; concurrent requests can observe the backend mid-swap, serving missing or double-loaded translations
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both describe a race condition on the shared @loaded_locales state: it is lazily/check-then-act initialized/updated in ensure_loaded! and can be accessed concurrently by multiple threads without synchronization, leading to inconsistent translation loading.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Initializer comment references config/initializers/02-freedom_patches.rb which does not exist; the actual ordering guarantee comes from config/application.rb, so the comment misleads maintainers and reordering per it breaks boot

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a comment in `config/initializers/i18n.rb` saying `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`, but the PR diff does not show the initializer list or whether `config/initializers/02-freedom_patches.rb` exists, nor does it show `config/application.rb` or any ordering mechanism. The claim that the referenced file "does not exist" and that reordering "breaks boot" cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n.ensure_loaded! exists only via an out-of-tree monkey patch (translate_accelerator.rb), not the i18n gem, creating a hard undocumented dependency that raises NoMethodError if the patch isn't applied first

adjudication.rationale: The new initializer defines `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` which calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!(l)`, and `ApplicationController#set_locale` now triggers this via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. In this diff there is no definition of `I18n.ensure_loaded!`; the only related addition is `ensure_loaded!(locale)` on `TranslateAccelerator` (a local freedom patch), implying this relies on nonstandard/monkey-patched behavior and ordering rather than the i18n gem API. That’s a real, diff-grounded maintainability/fragility concern, though whether it actually raises `NoMethodError` can’t be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash and overrides [] but not []=, so custom per-locale fallbacks registered via the standard API are silently discarded on every read

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `#[]` to always compute `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and does not consult the underlying hash storage. While `[]=` is inherited, any values written via `I18n.fallbacks[locale] = ...` would never be returned because reads ignore stored entries. The diff doesn’t show any code that relies on per-locale registrations, so it’s a real API/compatibility concern introduced by this design rather than a directly verifiable broken behavior in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SiteSetting.default_locale is evaluated lazily inside [], causing DB/cache access during translation misses which can crash background jobs, mailer deliveries, boot-time plugin calls, and rake tasks on fresh installs

adjudication.rationale: The new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` computes fallbacks as `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` (config/initializers/i18n.rb), so `SiteSetting.default_locale` is evaluated on each fallback lookup rather than being precomputed. That is diff-grounded and implies DB/cache-coupled access during translation fallback resolution (e.g., on misses). However, the claim that this "can crash background jobs/mailer/boot-time tasks" is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests in the diff for a behavior change affecting every translated string: fallback resolution regression could ship undetected, and fallback ordering and environment-level fallback deletion are unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes a broad behavior change to I18n fallback handling: it removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from multiple environments, adds a new initializer wiring `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and a custom fallback order (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`), and introduces new runtime loading behavior via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` plus `TranslateAccelerator#ensure_loaded!`. No corresponding tests are added in the diff to verify fallback ordering or prevent regressions from the environment-level removal, so this is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallback resolution with no handling for missing current-site context, breaking boot/migrations/rake jobs that translate before a site scope is established

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `FallbackLocaleList#[]` that always calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` when computing fallbacks (config/initializers/i18n.rb). There is no guard for contexts where `SiteSetting` may be unavailable or not yet initialized (e.g., during boot/task execution). The diff also makes fallback loading happen in `ApplicationController#set_locale` via `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, which will invoke `[]` and thus `SiteSetting.default_locale`. Whether this definitively breaks boot/migrations/rake cannot be verified from the diff alone (depends on `SiteSetting` behavior), but the concern is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! is only invoked on the web-request path, so background jobs, ActionMailer deliveries, MessageBus/SSR paths, and console/rake contexts fall back to slow translate_no_cache/lazy-load per lookup

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, but the claim that other contexts will "fall back to slow translate_no_cache/lazy-load per lookup" is not supported. `TranslateAccelerator#translate` already lazily loads the current locale once (`load_locale(config.locale) unless @loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)`), and `translate_no_cache` is triggered by `args.length > 0`, not by whether `ensure_loaded!` ran. The diff doesn’t show that background jobs/mailers/console would be forced into per-lookup slow paths; at most they wouldn’t eagerly preload fallback locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Locale fallback loading only occurs inside set_locale which runs only for web requests; background jobs, mailers, oneboxes, cron, and console code using I18n.t get missing translations because TranslateAccelerator#translate only loads config.locale

adjudication.rationale: While the diff does add `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, the claim that non-web contexts will get missing translations because `TranslateAccelerator#translate` “only loads config.locale” misreads how fallbacks work: when the fallbacks backend retries a lookup it calls `translate` again with the fallback locale, making `config.locale` equal to that fallback locale, and `TranslateAccelerator#translate` will then load that locale via `load_locale(config.locale)`. The controller call appears to be an eager-loading/perf optimization, not required for correctness, and the diff does not show that fallback translations would be missing elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Global I18n.fallbacks assignment in the initializer changes dev/test behavior by enabling fallbacks there, since fallbacks were previously gated to production-like environments via config.i18n.fallbacks in production.rb/profile.rb; this breaks tests asserting missing translations

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` from `production.rb`/`profile.rb` and instead globally mixes in `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` and assigns `I18n.fallbacks = FallbackLocaleList.new` in a new initializer (`config/initializers/i18n.rb`). That makes fallbacks behavior apply across all environments (including dev/test), whereas previously it was only enabled in certain environments via environment configs. The claim that this will "break tests" can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the cross-environment behavior change is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! runs on every request and FallbackLocaleList#[] allocates a fresh array and re-reads SiteSetting.default_locale each call, plus the loaded-check and chain-construction are split across two files that must be kept in sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` inside `ApplicationController#set_locale`, which is typically executed per request, so the call will run on every request. `FallbackLocaleList#[]` (in the new `config/initializers/i18n.rb`) builds a new array each call and reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` each time, which is a concrete per-call allocation/lookup cost. Also, `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` relies on `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, whose implementation is introduced separately in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`, creating cross-file coupling that must remain consistent. These are real, diff-grounded performance/maintainability concerns but not a verifiable correctness bug by themselves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Subclassing Hash to impersonate I18n.fallbacks only implements the [] method; plugins or Rails upgrades calling defaults, insert, or per-locale mutation (e.g. I18n.fallbacks[:de] = ...) will crash with NoMethodError or TypeError

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` and overrides `[]`, but because it subclasses `Hash` it still has standard `Hash` methods like `defaults`, `insert`, and `[]=`. A call such as `I18n.fallbacks[:de] = ...` would not inherently raise `NoMethodError`/`TypeError` based on this code (though the overridden `[]` would ignore stored values). The finding’s claim about crashes from missing methods is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallbacks module included via I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks) is dead code on the hot path because TranslateAccelerator's own class-level translate method shadows the module's translate; fallback only works accidentally via the super chain in translate_no_cache and could silently break on refactor

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows I18n::Backend::Fallbacks being included into `I18n.backend.class` (new `config/initializers/i18n.rb`) and an added `ensure_loaded!` method on `TranslateAccelerator` (lib patch), but it does not show that `TranslateAccelerator` is the active `I18n.backend` or that its `translate` method “shadows” the fallbacks module’s `translate`. The finding also references `translate_no_cache` behavior and a super-chain dependency that are not shown in this diff, so the claim cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback behavior should live in TranslateAccelerator (which owns translate) rather than bolted on via include where it is overridden

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds fallbacks by `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, while `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` defines its own `translate` method (and does not obviously delegate to `super`). In Ruby, a method defined on the class will take precedence over an included module’s method, so there is a concrete risk that fallback behavior implemented by the included module won’t actually be applied because `TranslateAccelerator` “owns” `translate`. This is a diff-grounded design/correctness concern about where fallback logic should be implemented/ensured (inside the accelerator vs. relying on an include).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Process-global cache keyed only by [locale, key] with no site dimension causes cross-site cache poisoning of fallback results in multisite, since default_locale varies per site

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a custom `I18n.fallbacks` implementation that dynamically consults `SiteSetting.default_locale` (`FallbackLocaleList#[]`) and an `ensure_loaded!` helper in `translate_accelerator.rb`, but it does not show any process-global translation result cache keyed only by `[locale, key]` or any caching of fallback *results* across sites. Without evidence in the diff of such a cache or its keying scheme, the claimed cross-site cache poisoning cannot be verified from these changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList Hash subclass silently discards writes: []= and merge! store entries never read back because [] is overridden, so plugin/gem fallback configuration is silently ignored

adjudication.rationale: In config/initializers/i18n.rb, FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but overrides `[]` to always return a computed array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` and never calls `super`. Any entries written via inherited `[]=` or `merge!` would be stored in the underlying Hash but never read back because reads always go through the overridden `[]`. Since the diff also replaces `I18n.fallbacks` with `FallbackLocaleList.new`, any external fallback configuration that relies on `I18n.fallbacks[loc]=...` / `merge!` would be effectively ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, so background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and scripts run fallbacks against unloaded locale data, bypassing the accelerator and leaving @loaded_locales unpopulated

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new preloading hook `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is added only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. The new fallback implementation (`FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!`) relies on `I18n.ensure_loaded!(l)` (supported by the newly added `ensure_loaded!(locale)` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`) to populate `@loaded_locales` for fallback locales. Since no other call sites are shown, non-controller execution paths (e.g., jobs/rake/mailers) would not run this explicit fallback-locale preloading step, which is a real scope/architecture gap introduced by the change, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes broken translations in those contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback terminal anchor changed from I18n.default_locale to hardcoded :en, breaking the documented invariant that the site's default locale is the terminal fallback

adjudication.rationale: The new fallback order is explicitly `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, making `:en` the last-resort fallback rather than the site default locale. This is a real behavior change compared to the previous `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (which would fall back to `I18n.default_locale`). Whether this “breaks a documented invariant” isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the terminal fallback being hardcoded to `:en` is diff-grounded and could be an intentional product decision rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym raises NoMethodError when settings store is not connected at translation time (rake tasks, migrations, early boot), converting missing translations into exceptions

adjudication.rationale: The new `FallbackLocaleList#[]` unconditionally calls `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). If `SiteSetting.default_locale` is `nil` (or otherwise unavailable during early boot/task execution), this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil.to_sym`) while computing fallbacks, which is a behavior change introduced by this diff (previously `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` did not depend on `SiteSetting`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: I18n::Backend::Simple.send(:include, ...) relies on initializer load order enforced only by a comment, so backend replacement (e.g. caching backend) can silently disable fallbacks

adjudication.rationale: The new initializer `config/initializers/i18n.rb` does mix in fallbacks via `I18n.backend.class.send(:include, I18n::Backend::Fallbacks)`, but the finding’s claim that load order is enforced *only by a comment* isn’t supported: Rails initializers run in filename order, and `i18n.rb` will naturally load after `02-freedom_patches.rb` (as the comment notes). Also, the diff does not show any later backend replacement (e.g., swapping to a caching backend) that would “silently disable fallbacks,” so that part is speculative beyond what’s verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Replacing I18n.fallbacks with a Hash subclass breaks the i18n gem Fallbacks API; I18n.t with fallbacks: option raises ArgumentError instead of honoring per-call fallback overrides

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the standard fallbacks setup (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true`) with a custom `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` assigned to `I18n.fallbacks` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). This deviates from the typical i18n/rails expectation that `I18n.fallbacks` is an `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`-like object and may break compatibility for callers or internal code that rely on the full Fallbacks API beyond `[]`. However, the specific claim that `I18n.t` with a per-call `fallbacks:` option will raise `ArgumentError` is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every fallback lookup, making translation a hard DB dependency that crashes (NoMethodError/ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid) during db:migrate on a fresh DB, assets:precompile without a DB, or rolling deploys before migrations finish, unlike the old static config.i18n.fallbacks = true

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `FallbackLocaleList#[]` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, which builds the fallback chain using `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` on every lookup (`[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`). This is a new runtime dependency on `SiteSetting` in the i18n fallback mechanism, whereas the removed `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` was static. Whether this definitively crashes during `db:migrate`/`assets:precompile` can’t be verified from the diff alone (depends on how `SiteSetting` is implemented/loaded and when fallbacks are invoked), but the coupling/perf/boot-order risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback chain changed from static I18n.default_locale (:en) to mutable SiteSetting.default_locale, so admins changing default_locale silently alters fallback text site-wide for every user with no migration, announcement, rollback, or opt-out setting

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` (which falls back to `I18n.default_locale`) with a custom `FallbackLocaleList` where the fallback chain is `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]` (config/initializers/i18n.rb). That means changing `SiteSetting.default_locale` will immediately affect fallback behavior site-wide. The finding’s broader claims about needing migration/announcement/rollback aren’t verifiable from the diff, but the core behavior change to a mutable admin setting is real and worth review as an intentional/communicated change rather than a direct defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: translate_accelerator.rb's translate method dereferences @loaded_locales directly without the ||= [] guard used in ensure_loaded!, causing NoMethodError: undefined method 'include?' for nil if translate is called before ensure_loaded!/load_locale

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb`, the `translate` method calls `@loaded_locales.include?(config.locale)` but, in the diff shown, only the newly added `ensure_loaded!` method initializes `@loaded_locales` via `@loaded_locales ||= []`. If `translate` can run before any code path that sets `@loaded_locales` (e.g., before `ensure_loaded!`/`load_locale` has initialized it), this would raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.include?`. The diff does not show any other initialization of `@loaded_locales`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fallback locales are only loaded inside the request cycle via set_locale, so fallback lookups outside controllers (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer, console, scripts) silently return 'translation missing' because the accelerator only loads config.locale and never loads fallback locales like :en

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`, meaning fallback locale files are proactively loaded only during controller requests. The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` explicitly calls `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each fallback locale, but nothing in the diff invokes this outside the request cycle. Meanwhile `TranslateAccelerator#translate` still only ensures `config.locale` is loaded, and does not load fallback locales automatically; thus fallback lookups in non-controller contexts (e.g., Sidekiq/ActionMailer/console) can hit unloaded fallback locales (like `:en`) and yield missing translations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FallbackLocaleList overrides Hash#[] to always compute a fresh list, so any code mutating the fallbacks hash (I18n.fallbacks[:de] << :fr or assignment) is silently dropped with no error or effect

adjudication.rationale: In `config/initializers/i18n.rb`, `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides `def [](locale)` to always return a freshly computed array `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` and does not consult or store any underlying hash state. As a result, mutations like `I18n.fallbacks[:de] << :fr` would only mutate a temporary array and won’t persist, and `[]=` assignments won’t be reflected by later `[]` calls. The diff doesn’t show such mutations occurring, so it’s more of a semantic/maintainability trap than a proven runtime defect here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ensure_loaded! check-then-act on the shared @loaded_locales array races under multi-threaded request handling; concurrent requests can observe the backend mid-swap, serving missing or double-loaded translations
matched_golden_ids: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a race condition on the shared @loaded_locales state: it is lazily/check-then-act initialized/updated in ensure_loaded! and can be accessed concurrently by multiple threads without synchronization, leading to inconsistent translation loading.
